notes: High-level: mid-market product team building an in-app onboarding copilot — goal is consistent sub-200ms perceived latency for streaming first-token + tool-calls.
POC scope: 2-week hosted API pilot using streaming + function calling for 3 guided flows (signup, first-project, billing setup).
Token economics: strict per-session token cap (900–1200 tokens/session target) — product team wants firm token caps enforced server-side.
Quote from Head of Product: "We need predictable cost per user and no surprises on big help flows. If latency spikes, conversion drops."
Interested in intelligent fallback routing: smaller model for low-cost responses, upgrade to larger model when user intent = deep help (detect via heuristic).
Security ask: SSO (SAML), audit logs retained 13 months, keys via customer KMS; data residency preference: US-only for first year.
Pricing: asked for hosted usage estimate + committed-Dedicated delta and a model for committed burst capacity during onboarding campaigns.
POC metrics requested: p50/p95 token latency for streaming first-byte, end-to-end response time for tool-invocations, tokens/sec throughput under 50 concurrent sessions.
Internal stakeholders: Head of Product (Eva Marin), Eng Manager (Daniel Chu), Security Lead (Marcus Lee). AE asked to include Solutions Eng + Infra for demo.
Red flags called out: current security checklist flagged data residency and KMS integration; procurement will require SOC2 Type II evidence and SLAs before Dedicated commitment.
Quick wins: Redwood streaming demo + sample function-calling integration using their sample web widget; show token capping and cold-start latency numbers.
Requested artifacts: pricing spreadsheet, SLA grid, latency/throughput runbook, sample rollout plan for canary + fallback to smaller model.

use_case_summary: In-app guided onboarding copilot: short guided chat flows that call product tooling (create-project API, billing helper) via function calls. Primary constraints are consistent streaming latency (<200ms perceived for first token), strict token caps per session, predictable unit cost. Scale target: 50 concurrent onboarding flows during campaigns; spike tolerance for marketing-driven bursts.
requirements: Token-capping enforcement and per-session budget controls
